title: Witnessed VF arrest - ROSC to STEMI
objectives: Pit-crew roles assigned in first 60 s; CC as code commander
Shocks without delay; compressions resume immediately
AEMT meds/airway timing: epi after 1st cycle (shockable), q every other cycle; SGA after 8 min
Recognize ROSC on capno; post-ROSC ventilation 10/min, EtCO2 35-45, SpO2 94-98
resources: AED/monitor, BVM, OPA, SGA, IV/IO, epi 0.1 mg/mL x4, NS, capno, metronome, 12-lead. UVMMC (PCI) ~5 min
dispatch: UVM Rescue and Engine 2, respond to Green Mountain Fitness, 220 Main St, for a 56-year-old male collapsed, CPR in progress. Gym AED on scene. Time out 0612.

scene.location: Gym floor between treadmills. Bright, space is tight - move equipment.
scene.setup: Manikin supine, staff member doing CPR, gym AED attached (1 shock delivered before arrival).
scene.roles: Bystander CPR (gym staff); 2 FD EMRs arrive with crew; evaluator calls rhythms.

patient.name: Paul Desrochers
patient.on_arrival: Unresponsive, apneic/agonal, pulseless. Bystander CPR adequate depth, rate ~90.

SAMPLE: Collapse 0608 witnessed; CPR started 0609; AED shock 0611

primary: No trauma, no medic alert, no DNR
Witnessed VF arrest with bystander CPR - **high survival potential**
secondary: HTN, lisinopril, smoker, "chest tightness this week"
vitals_note: Arrest stages are 2-min cycles from EMS contact. Pulse 0 = CPR.

vitals.other: **VF** - shock #3 total. Epi #1 after this cycle (IV/IO)
Point to capno; no ROSC until fixed
Occasional PVCs. Gags on SGA - reassess airway

flow.give: Bystander CPR in progress, gym AED attached, 1 shock given. Stage **A**.
expected: Pit-crew roles assigned (3.6), CC = code commander
Crew's monitor/AED swapped w/o long pause

flow.give: Call VF at each analysis. Watch hands-off time.

branches.if: Crew monitor battery dies at T+6
branches.then: switch back to gym AED; CPR gap must stay < 10 s

flow.give: Stage **B**. Wife arrives at T+15 (cue if CC isn't talking to family).
expected: Epi 1 mg (0.1 mg/mL) after 1st cycle, then q every other cycle

branches.if: Crew loads with CPR in progress ("UVMMC is 5 min")
branches.then: debrief 8.17: resuscitate on scene; moving CPR is poor

flow.give: After shock #4 -> EtCO2 jumps to 44. Stage **D** on pulse check.
expected: SGA if not placed (after 8 min) / maintain airway

flow.give: Show **12-lead** card. Give Stage **E** or **F** based on vent rate.
expected: SBP < 90 -> NS 500 mL; MD for more

branches.then: back to 3.2A: shock, CPR; work it in open space

expected: Report: downtime, shocks, epi doses, ROSC time

critical: Roles not assigned / no code commander
Epi wrong concentration (1 mg/mL IV) or wrong timing
SGA placed during first 8 min with patent airway
ROSC not recognized; or CPR continued on pulse
No post-ROSC 12-lead / STEMI ALERT to UVMMC
differentials: Chest rubbing pre-collapse, exertion, risk factors, post-ROSC STE
debrief: How did you assign roles and who watched CPR quality?
What did capnography tell you during and after the arrest?
Why epi after the first cycle in VF but ASAP in asystole?
Post-ROSC: what are your ventilation, SpO2 and BP targets?
Why work the arrest on scene when UVMMC is 5 min away?

crew_card.dispatch: Green Mountain Fitness, 220 Main St. 56 y/o M collapsed, CPR in progress. Gym AED on scene.
crew_card.on_arrival: Man on gym floor between treadmills. Staff member doing CPR, gym AED attached. Crowd watching.

actor_card.Gym staff: Doing CPR (a bit slow). "The AED shocked him once. He was rubbing his chest, then went down."
actor_card.Wife (T+15): Arrives frantic. "Is he alive?" Gives history only if someone talks to her.
actor_card.Evaluator: Call rhythm only at analysis. ROSC only after shock #4 AND acceptable CPR quality.
